passages.text: When Jesus had concluded His discourse in the hearing of the people, He went to Capernaum.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He finished all His words.
The people listened to Him.
After this, Jesus went to Capernaum.
passages.original: Ἐπειδὴ ἐπλήρωσεν πάντα τὰ ῥήματα αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰς ἀκοὰς τοῦ λαοῦ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς Καφαρναούμ

passages.text: There a highly valued servant of a centurion was sick and about to die.
passages.sermon:
A centurion had a servant.
The servant was very important to the centurion.
The servant was sick.
The servant was about to die.
passages.original: Ἑκατοντάρχου δέ τινος δοῦλος κακῶς ἔχων ἤμελλεν τελευτᾶν ὃς ἦν αὐτῷ ἔντιμος

passages.text: When the centurion heard about Jesus, he sent some Jewish elders to ask Him to come and heal his servant.
passages.sermon:
A centurion lived in Capernaum.
He had a servant who was very sick.
The servant was about to die.
The centurion heard about Jesus.
He wanted Jesus to help his servant.
The centurion did not go to Jesus himself.
He sent some Jewish elders to Jesus.
He asked the elders to speak to Jesus for him.
He wanted Jesus to come and heal his servant.
passages.original: ἀκούσας δὲ περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς αὐτὸν πρεσβυτέρους τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐρωτῶν αὐτὸν ὅπως ἐλθὼν διασώσῃ τὸν δοῦλον αὐτοῦ

passages.text: They came to Jesus and pleaded with Him earnestly, “This man is worthy to have You grant this, for he loves our nation and has built our synagogue.”
passages.sermon:
Some Jewish elders came to Jesus.
They pleaded with Jesus earnestly.
They said, “This man is worthy for You to help him.
He loves our nation.
He built our synagogue for us.”
passages.original: οἱ δὲ παραγενόμενοι πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν σπουδαίως λέγοντες ὅτι Ἄξιός ἐστιν ᾧ παρέξῃ τοῦτο ἀγαπᾷ γὰρ τὸ ἔθνος ἡμῶν καὶ τὴν συναγωγὴν αὐτὸς ᾠκοδόμησεν ἡμῖν

passages.text: So Jesus went with them. But when He was not far from the house, the centurion sent friends with the message: “Lord, do not trouble Yourself, for I am not worthy to have You come under my roof.
passages.sermon:
Jesus went with the Jewish elders.
He walked with them toward the centurion’s house.
Jesus was not far from the house.
The centurion was a Roman officer.
He sent his friends to meet Jesus.
The friends brought a message from the centurion.
They said, “Lord, do not trouble Yourself.”
The centurion said, “I am not worthy for You to come under my roof.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐπορεύετο σὺν αὐτοῖς ἤδη δὲ αὐτοῦ οὐ μακρὰν ἀπέχοντος ἀπὸ τῆς οἰκίας ἔπεμψεν φίλους ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης λέγων αὐτῷ Κύριε μὴ σκύλλου οὐ γὰρ ἱκανός εἰμι ἵνα ὑπὸ τὴν στέγην μου εἰσέλθῃς

passages.text: That is why I did not consider myself worthy to come to You. But just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
passages.sermon:
The centurion was a Roman officer.
He did not think he was worthy to come to Jesus.
He sent a message to Jesus.
He said, “That is why I did not consider myself worthy to come to You.”
He asked Jesus to speak a word.
He believed that if Jesus spoke, his servant would be healed.
passages.original: διὸ οὐδὲ ἐμαυτὸν ἠξίωσα πρὸς σὲ ἐλθεῖν ἀλλὰ εἰπὲ λόγῳ καὶ ἰαθήτω ὁ παῖς μου

passages.text: For I myself am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I tell one to go, and he goes; and another to come, and he comes. I tell my servant to do something, and he does it.”
passages.sermon:
The centurion spoke about himself.
He said, “I am a man under authority.
I have soldiers under me.
I give orders to my soldiers.
I tell one soldier, ‘Go.’
He goes.
I tell another soldier, ‘Come.’
He comes.
I tell my servant, ‘Do this.’
He does it.”
passages.original: καὶ γὰρ ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπός εἰμι ὑπὸ ἐξουσίαν τασσόμενος ἔχων ὑπ’ ἐμαυτὸν στρατιώτας καὶ λέγω τούτῳ Πορεύθητι καὶ πορεύεται καὶ ἄλλῳ Ἔρχου καὶ ἔρχεται καὶ τῷ δούλῳ μου Ποίησον τοῦτο καὶ ποιεῖ

passages.text: When Jesus heard this, He marveled at the centurion. Turning to the crowd following Him, He said, “I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such great faith.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus listened to the centurion’s words.
Jesus felt amazed at the centurion.
A crowd was following Jesus.
Jesus turned to this crowd.
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus said, “I tell you the truth.
I have not found such great faith even in Israel.”
passages.original: Ἀκούσας δὲ ταῦτα ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐθαύμασεν αὐτόν καὶ στραφεὶς τῷ ἀκολουθοῦντι αὐτῷ ὄχλῳ εἶπεν Λέγω ὑμῖν οὐδὲ ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ τοσαύτην πίστιν εὗρον

passages.text: And when the messengers returned to the house, they found the servant in good health.
passages.sermon: The messengers returned to the house.\r\nThey found the servant in good health.
passages.original: καὶ ὑποστρέψαντες εἰς τὸν οἶκον οἱ πεμφθέντες εὗρον τὸν δοῦλον ὑγιαίνοντα

passages.text: Soon afterward, Jesus went to a town called Nain. His disciples went with Him, accompanied by a large crowd.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Soon after these events, Jesus traveled to a town.
The town was called Nain.
Jesus’ disciples went with Him.
A large crowd also followed Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἑξῆς ἐπορεύθη εἰς πόλιν καλουμένην Ναΐν καὶ συνεπορεύοντο αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ ὄχλος πολύς

passages.text: As He approached the town gate, He saw a dead man being carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow. And a large crowd from the town was with her.
passages.sermon:
Jesus approached the gate of the town called Nain.
He saw people carrying out a dead man.
This dead man was the only son of his mother.
His mother was a widow.
A large crowd from the town was with her.
passages.original: ὡς δὲ ἤγγισεν τῇ πύλῃ τῆς πόλεως καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐξεκομίζετο τεθνηκὼς μονογενὴς υἱὸς τῇ μητρὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ αὐτὴ ἦν χήρα καὶ ὄχλος τῆς πόλεως ἱκανὸς ἦν σὺν αὐτῇ

passages.text: When the Lord saw her, He had compassion on her and said, “Do not weep.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Lord.
Jesus saw the woman.
The woman was a widow.
Her only son had died.
Jesus felt compassion for her.
Jesus spoke to her.
Jesus said, “Do not weep.”
passages.original: καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὴν ὁ Κύριος ἐσπλαγχνίσθη ἐπ’ αὐτῇ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ Μὴ κλαῖε

passages.text: Then He went up and touched the coffin, and those carrying it stood still. “Young man,” He said, “I tell you, get up!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus walked up to the coffin.
He touched the coffin.
The men carrying the coffin stopped.
Jesus spoke to the dead man.
Jesus said, “Young man, I tell you, get up!”
passages.original: Καὶ προσελθὼν ἥψατο τῆς σοροῦ οἱ δὲ βαστάζοντες ἔστησαν καὶ εἶπεν Νεανίσκε σοὶ λέγω ἐγέρθητι

passages.text: And the dead man sat up and began to speak! Then Jesus gave him back to his mother.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw a dead man.
Jesus spoke to the dead man.
The dead man sat up.
The dead man began to speak.
Jesus gave the man back to his mother.
passages.original: καὶ ἀνεκάθισεν ὁ νεκρὸς καὶ ἤρξατο λαλεῖν καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὸν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: A sense of awe swept over all of them, and they glorified God. “A great prophet has appeared among us!” they said. “God has visited His people!”
passages.sermon:
All the people felt awe.
They honored God.
They said, “A great prophet has appeared among us.”
They also said, “God has visited His people.”
passages.original: Ἔλαβεν δὲ φόβος πάντας καὶ ἐδόξαζον τὸν Θεὸν λέγοντες ὅτι Προφήτης μέγας ἠγέρθη ἐν ἡμῖν καὶ ὅτι Ἐπεσκέψατο ὁ Θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: And the news about Jesus spread throughout Judea and all the surrounding region.
passages.sermon:
Jesus raised a dead man to life.
\r\nPeople saw this miracle.
\r\nNews about Jesus spread everywhere.
\r\nPeople in all Judea heard about Jesus.
\r\nPeople in every surrounding region also heard about Jesus.
passages.original: καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ λόγος οὗτος ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ περὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ πάσῃ τῇ περιχώρῳ

passages.text: Then John’s disciples informed him about all these things.
passages.sermon: John had disciples.\r\nJohn’s disciples learned about these events.\r\nJohn’s disciples told John about all these things.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν Ἰωάννῃ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ περὶ πάντων τούτων

passages.text: So John called two of his disciples and sent them to ask the Lord, “Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?”
passages.sermon:
John was a prophet.
\r\nJohn had disciples.
\r\nJohn called two of his disciples.
\r\nJohn sent these two disciples to the Lord.
\r\nJohn gave them a question to ask.
\r\nJohn told them to ask the Lord, “Are you the One who was to come?”
\r\nJohn also told them to ask, “Should we look for someone else?”
passages.original: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος δύο τινὰς τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ὁ Ἰωάννης ἔπεμψεν πρὸς τὸν Κύριον λέγων Σὺ εἶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἢ ἄλλον προσδοκῶμεν

passages.text: When the men came to Jesus, they said, “John the Baptist sent us to ask, ‘Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?’ ”
passages.sermon:
John the Baptist was a prophet.
John the Baptist had disciples.
John the Baptist sent two of his disciples to Jesus.
The two men came to Jesus.
The men spoke to Jesus.
They said, “John the Baptist sent us to you.”
They said, “He asks, ‘Are you the One who was to come?’”
They said, “Or should we look for someone else?”
passages.original: Παραγενόμενοι δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ ἄνδρες εἶπαν Ἰωάννης ὁ Βαπτιστὴς ἀπέστειλεν ἡμᾶς πρὸς σὲ λέγων Σὺ εἶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἢ ἄλλον προσδοκῶμεν

passages.text: At that very hour Jesus healed many people of their diseases, afflictions, and evil spirits, and He gave sight to many who were blind.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood there at that moment.
He healed many people.
He took away their diseases.
He removed their afflictions.
He cast out evil spirits from many people.
He gave sight to many blind people.
passages.original: Ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἐθεράπευσεν πολλοὺς ἀπὸ νόσων καὶ μαστίγων καὶ πνευμάτων πονηρῶν καὶ τυφλοῖς πολλοῖς ἐχαρίσατο βλέπειν

passages.text: So He replied, “Go back and report to John what you have seen and heard: The blind receive sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the good news is preached to the poor.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the men who came from John the Baptist.
He told them to return to John.
He told them to report what they saw and heard.
Blind people now see.
Lame people now walk.
Lepers are now cleansed.
Deaf people now hear.
Dead people are now raised.
The good news is now preached to the poor.
passages.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Πορευθέντες ἀπαγγείλατε Ἰωάννῃ ἃ εἴδετε καὶ ἠκούσατε τυφλοὶ ἀναβλέπουσιν χωλοὶ περιπατοῦσιν λεπροὶ καθαρίζονται καὶ κωφοὶ ἀκούουσιν νεκροὶ ἐγείρονται πτωχοὶ εὐαγγελίζονται

passages.text: Blessed is the one who does not fall away on account of Me.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the people.\r\nHe said, “Blessed is the person who does not fall away because of Me.”
passages.original: καὶ μακάριός ἐστιν ὃς ἐὰν μὴ σκανδαλισθῇ ἐν ἐμοί

passages.text: After John’s messengers had left, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed swaying in the wind?
passages.sermon:
John had messengers.
The messengers left.
Jesus spoke to the crowds.
Jesus spoke about John.
Jesus asked the crowds a question.
He said, "What did you go out into the wilderness to see?"
He asked, "Did you go to see a reed swaying in the wind?"
passages.original: Ἀπελθόντων δὲ τῶν ἀγγέλων Ἰωάννου ἤρξατο λέγειν πρὸς τοὺς ὄχλους περὶ Ἰωάννου Τί ἐξήλθατε εἰς τὴν ἔρημον θεάσασθαι κάλαμον ὑπὸ ἀνέμου σαλευόμενον

passages.text: Otherwise, what did you go out to see? A man dressed in fine clothes? Look, those who wear elegant clothing and live in luxury are found in palaces.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the crowds about John.
He asked them a question.
He said, "What did you go out to see?"
He asked, "Did you go to see a man wearing fine clothes?"
He explained about people who wear fine clothes.
He said, "People who wear elegant clothing live in palaces."
He showed that John was not like those people.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ τί ἐξήλθατε ἰδεῖν ἄνθρωπον ἐν μαλακοῖς ἱματίοις ἠμφιεσμένον ἰδοὺ οἱ ἐν ἱματισμῷ ἐνδόξῳ καὶ τρυφῇ ὑπάρχοντες ἐν τοῖς βασιλείοις εἰσίν

passages.text: What then did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the crowds about John.
He asked them a question.
He said, "What did you go out to see?"
He asked, "Did you go to see a prophet?"
He answered, "Yes, I tell you, you saw a prophet."
He said, "John is more than a prophet."
passages.original: Ἀλλὰ τί ἐξήλθατε ἰδεῖν προφήτην ναί λέγω ὑμῖν καὶ περισσότερον προφήτου

passages.text: This is the one about whom it is written: ‘Behold, I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way before You.’
passages.sermon: John is the person written about in Scripture.\r\nGod said, “I will send my messenger ahead of you.”\r\nThis messenger will prepare your way before you.
passages.original: οὗτός ἐστιν περὶ οὗ γέγραπται Ἰδοὺ ἀποστέλλω τὸν ἄγγελόν μου πρὸ προσώπου σου Ὃς κατασκευάσει τὴν ὁδόν σου ἔμπροσθέν σου

passages.text: I tell you, among those born of women there is no one greater than John, yet even the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus said, “No one born of a woman is greater than John.
John is the greatest among all people born naturally.
But the least person in the kingdom of God is greater than John.
The kingdom of God is greater than anything on earth.
Even the smallest person in God’s kingdom has a higher place than John.”
passages.original: Λέγω ὑμῖν μείζων ἐν γεννητοῖς γυναικῶν Ἰωάννου οὐδείς ἐστιν ὁ δὲ μικρότερος ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ Θεοῦ μείζων αὐτοῦ ἐστιν

passages.text: All the people who heard this, even the tax collectors, acknowledged God’s justice. For they had received the baptism of John.
passages.sermon:
All the people heard this.
The tax collectors also heard this.
They received the baptism of John.
They acknowledged that God is just.
passages.original: Καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ἀκούσας καὶ οἱ τελῶναι ἐδικαίωσαν τὸν Θεόν βαπτισθέντες τὸ βάπτισμα Ἰωάννου

passages.text: But the Pharisees and experts in the law rejected God’s purpose for themselves, because they had not been baptized by John.
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees were religious leaders.
The experts in the law studied and taught God’s commands.
These men rejected God’s purpose for themselves.
They did not accept what God wanted for them.
They refused to be baptized by John.
Their refusal showed they did not follow God’s plan.
passages.original: οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ νομικοὶ τὴν βουλὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἠθέτησαν εἰς ἑαυτούς μὴ βαπτισθέντες ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: “To what, then, can I compare the men of this generation? What are they like?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people of his time.
He asked a question about them.
He said, “What can I compare the people of this generation to?
What are they like?”
passages.original: Τίνι οὖν ὁμοιώσω τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ τίνι εἰσὶν ὅμοιοι

passages.text: They are like children sitting in the marketplace and calling out to one another: ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not weep.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke about the people of his generation.
He said they are like children.
These children sit in the marketplace.
They call out to each other.
They say, “We played the flute for you.
But you did not dance.”
They also say, “We sang a sad song.
But you did not weep.”
passages.original: ὅμοιοί εἰσιν παιδίοις τοῖς ἐν ἀγορᾷ καθημένοις καὶ προσφωνοῦσιν ἀλλήλοις ἃ λέγει Ηὐλήσαμεν ὑμῖν καὶ οὐκ ὠρχήσασθε Ἐθρηνήσαμεν καὶ οὐκ ἐκλαύσατε

passages.text: For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, ‘He has a demon!’
passages.sermon:
John the Baptist came.
He did not eat bread.
He did not drink wine.
You say, "He has a demon."
passages.original: Ἐλήλυθεν γὰρ Ἰωάννης ὁ Βαπτιστὴς μὴ ἐσθίων ἄρτον μήτε πίνων οἶνον καὶ λέγετε Δαιμόνιον ἔχει

passages.text: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and you say, ‘Look at this glutton and drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus came eating food.
Jesus came drinking wine.
You saw Jesus eating and drinking.
You said, “Look at this man!”
You called Jesus a glutton.
You called Jesus a drunkard.
You said Jesus is a friend of tax collectors.
You said Jesus is a friend of sinners.
passages.original: ἐλήλυθεν ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐσθίων καὶ πίνων καὶ λέγετε Ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος φάγος καὶ οἰνοπότης φίλος τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν

passages.text: But wisdom is vindicated by all her children.”
passages.sermon:
Wisdom is a quality that guides people to do what is right.
Children of wisdom are people who follow wisdom and act rightly.
All the children of wisdom show that wisdom is true and good.
Their actions prove that wisdom is right.
Wisdom receives honor and is shown to be correct by those who live by it.
passages.original: καὶ ἐδικαιώθη ἡ σοφία ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν τέκνων αὐτῆς

passages.text: Then one of the Pharisees invited Jesus to eat with him, and He entered the Pharisee’s house and reclined at the table.
passages.sermon:
A Pharisee invited Jesus to eat with him.
Jesus accepted the invitation.
Jesus entered the Pharisee’s house.
Jesus reclined at the table.
passages.original: Ἠρώτα δέ τις αὐτὸν τῶν Φαρισαίων ἵνα φάγῃ μετ’ αὐτοῦ καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ Φαρισαίου κατεκλίθη

passages.text: When a sinful woman from that town learned that Jesus was dining there, she brought an alabaster jar of perfume.
passages.sermon:
A woman lived in that town.
She was known as a sinner.
She learned that Jesus was dining in the Pharisee’s house.
She brought an alabaster jar of perfume.
passages.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ ἥτις ἦν ἐν τῇ πόλει ἁμαρτωλός καὶ ἐπιγνοῦσα ὅτι κατάκειται ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ τοῦ Φαρισαίου κομίσασα ἀλάβαστρον μύρου

passages.text: As she stood behind Him at His feet weeping, she began to wet His feet with her tears and wipe them with her hair. Then she kissed His feet and anointed them with the perfume.
passages.sermon:
A sinful woman stood behind Jesus.
She stood at His feet.
She wept.
Her tears fell on His feet.
She began to wet His feet with her tears.
She wiped His feet with her hair.
She kissed His feet.
She anointed His feet with perfume.
passages.original: καὶ στᾶσα ὀπίσω παρὰ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ κλαίουσα τοῖς δάκρυσιν ἤρξατο βρέχειν τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ καὶ ταῖς θριξὶν τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτῆς ἐξέμασσεν καὶ κατεφίλει τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ καὶ ἤλειφεν τῷ μύρῳ

passages.text: When the Pharisee who had invited Jesus saw this, he said to himself, “If this man were a prophet, He would know who this is and what kind of woman is touching Him—for she is a sinner!”
passages.sermon:
A Pharisee invited Jesus to his house.
The Pharisee saw a woman touching Jesus.
This woman was known as a sinner in the city.
The Pharisee spoke to himself.
He said, “If this man were a prophet, he would know who is touching him.
He would know what kind of woman she is.
She is a sinner.”
passages.original: Ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Φαρισαῖος ὁ καλέσας αὐτὸν εἶπεν ἐν ἑαυτῷ λέγων Οὗτος εἰ ἦν προφήτης ἐγίνωσκεν ἂν τίς καὶ ποταπὴ ἡ γυνὴ ἥτις ἅπτεται αὐτοῦ ὅτι ἁμαρτωλός ἐστιν

passages.text: But Jesus answered him, “Simon, I have something to tell you.” “Tell me, Teacher,” he said.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to Simon.\r\nJesus said, “Simon, I have something to tell you.”\r\nSimon replied, “Tell me, Teacher.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν Σίμων ἔχω σοί τι εἰπεῖν Ὁ δέ Διδάσκαλε εἰπέ φησίν

passages.text: “Two men were debtors to a certain moneylender. One owed him five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.
passages.sermon: A moneylender had two debtors.\r\nOne man owed the moneylender five hundred denarii.\r\nAnother man owed the moneylender fifty denarii.
passages.original: Δύο χρεοφειλέται ἦσαν δανιστῇ τινι ὁ εἷς ὤφειλεν δηνάρια πεντακόσια ὁ δὲ ἕτερος πεντήκοντα

passages.text: When they were unable to repay him, he forgave both of them. Which one, then, will love him more?”
passages.sermon:
The two men could not repay the moneylender.
The moneylender forgave both men.
Jesus asked Simon a question.
Jesus said, "Which man will love the moneylender more?"
passages.original: μὴ ἐχόντων αὐτῶν ἀποδοῦναι ἀμφοτέροις ἐχαρίσατο τίς οὖν αὐτῶν πλεῖον ἀγαπήσει αὐτόν

passages.text: “I suppose the one who was forgiven more,” Simon replied. “You have judged correctly,” Jesus said.
passages.sermon:
Simon replied to Jesus.
Simon said, “I suppose the one who was forgiven more will love him more.”
Jesus answered Simon.
Jesus said, “You have judged correctly.”
passages.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς Σίμων εἶπεν Ὑπολαμβάνω ὅτι ᾧ τὸ πλεῖον ἐχαρίσατο Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ὀρθῶς ἔκρινας

passages.text: And turning toward the woman, He said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? When I entered your house, you did not give Me water for My feet, but she wet My feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Simon.
Jesus turned toward the woman.
Jesus said, “Simon, do you see this woman?
I entered your house.
You did not give Me water for My feet.
This woman wet My feet with her tears.
She wiped My feet with her hair.”
passages.original: Καὶ στραφεὶς πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα τῷ Σίμωνι ἔφη Βλέπεις ταύτην τὴν γυναῖκα εἰσῆλθόν σου εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν ὕδωρ μοι ἐπὶ πόδας οὐκ ἔδωκας αὕτη δὲ τοῖς δάκρυσιν ἔβρεξέν μου τοὺς πόδας καὶ ταῖς θριξὶν αὐτῆς ἐξέμαξεν

passages.text: You did not greet Me with a kiss, but she has not stopped kissing My feet since I arrived.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Simon.
Jesus said, “You did not greet Me with a kiss.
This woman has kissed My feet.
She has not stopped kissing My feet since I arrived.”
passages.original: φίλημά μοι οὐκ ἔδωκας αὕτη δὲ ἀφ’ ἧς εἰσῆλθον οὐ διέλιπεν καταφιλοῦσά μου τοὺς πόδας

passages.text: You did not anoint My head with oil, but she has anointed My feet with perfume.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to Simon.\r\nJesus said, “You did not anoint My head with oil.\r\nThis woman anointed My feet with perfume.”
passages.original: ἐλαίῳ τὴν κεφαλήν μου οὐκ ἤλειψας αὕτη δὲ μύρῳ ἤλειψεν τοὺς πόδας μου

passages.text: Therefore I tell you, because her many sins have been forgiven, she has loved much. But he who has been forgiven little loves little.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Simon the Pharisee.
Jesus explained the woman’s actions.
The woman had many sins.
God forgave her many sins.
She showed great love.
A person who is forgiven little shows little love.
passages.original: οὗ χάριν λέγω σοι ἀφέωνται αἱ ἁμαρτίαι αὐτῆς αἱ πολλαί ὅτι ἠγάπησεν πολύ ᾧ δὲ ὀλίγον ἀφίεται ὀλίγον ἀγαπᾷ

passages.text: Then Jesus said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the woman.\r\nHe said, “Your sins are forgiven.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῇ Ἀφέωνταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι

passages.text: But those at the table began to say to themselves, “Who is this who even forgives sins?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus sat at the table with others.
The people at the table spoke quietly among themselves.
They asked a question about Jesus.
They said, “Who is this man?”
They saw that Jesus forgave sins.
They wondered how Jesus could forgive sins.
passages.original: Καὶ ἤρξαντο οἱ συνανακείμενοι λέγειν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς Τίς οὗτός ἐστιν ὃς καὶ ἁμαρτίας ἀφίησιν

passages.text: And Jesus told the woman, “Your faith has saved you; go in peace.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the woman.\r\nHe said, "Your faith has saved you."\r\nGo in peace.
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα Ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε πορεύου εἰς εἰρήνην
